name: example
context: A tiny Python greeting module, built incrementally. Plain Python 3, standard library only, no packaging.

tasks.spec: Create a file greet.py at the repository root containing exactly one function: greet(name: str) -> str, which returns the string 'Hello, <name>!' with <name> replaced by the argument. No main block, no prints, no other functions, no imports.
tasks.check: python3 -c "from greet import greet; assert greet('Tiamat') == 'Hello, Tiamat!'; import greet as m; assert m.__doc__ is None or True"
tasks.verified: greet.py imports and greet('Tiamat') returns exactly 'Hello, Tiamat!'

tasks.spec: greet.py already exists at the repository root with a greet(name) function. Add a second function shout(name: str) -> str that returns greet(name) uppercased (it must call greet, not rebuild the string). Change nothing else in the file.
tasks.check: python3 -c "from greet import greet, shout; assert shout('Tiamat') == 'HELLO, TIAMAT!'; assert greet('Tiamat') == 'Hello, Tiamat!'"
tasks.verified: shout('Tiamat') returns 'HELLO, TIAMAT!' and greet still works, via a shout that delegates to greet
